In this section, we provide justifications for selecting each test point and explain why it is crucial for evaluating HP- TES system performance. Base HP Space Conditioning without TES. Two cases each for heating and cooling mode (Tests #1 and #6) corresponded to the base HP providing space conditioning without TES. These cases are of significant importance, given that the TES is sized for a finite operating period (at least two continuous hours). Thus, the base HP mode will provide space conditioning for a vast majority of the day (e.g., up to 83% (10 hours) of a 12-hour working day). Therefore, the HP-TES system operating in steady-state base HP mode should not have degraded performance compared to a traditional HP (i.e., without TES). One “favorable” ambient condition (Test #1H = H1 condition; Test #6C = F condition), Full Full and one “unfavorable” ambient condition (Test #6H = H3 condition; Test #1C = A Full Full condition) are considered for base HP mode operating without TES.
